correctness.rationale: All \(n\ge5\) and all feasible occupancies covered: the standard intersecting-two-subset lemma shows independent families are stars or (only with 3 tokens) triangles. Every \(k\ge4\) state is frozen by a three-distinct-retained-leaves obstruction. The \(k=3\) slide relation is exactly star-triangle incidence and each two-step triangle passage is a Johnson \(J(n,3)\) edge, so the explicit all-pairs distance formula and eccentricities are proved combinatorially. For \(k=2\) a symmetry-reduced complete finite check of all 30 five-label and all 60 six-label configurations proves distance at most 4 on any pair-supported six-label subgraph, while disjoint-leaf same-center states require 4 moves. Verify.py independently constructs states from literal pairwise edge intersections and slides from disjoint replacements, checks all-source shortest paths for \(n=5\)..9 and all frozen states \(n=5\)..7; CHECKS.txt is actual run output. Finite checks are used only for the bounded \(n\le6\) computation, never as a substitute for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is a statement-level classification for all \(n\ge5\) of every occupancy and every three-token geodesic, not merely the standard extremal classification of pairwise-intersecting edges. The closest full primary papers (arXiv:1406.6576, arXiv:2203.16861, arXiv:2301.00317) develop tree algorithms, realization/structure of general slide graphs, and acyclic settings, respectively, without a \(\operatorname{KG}(n,2)\) all-occupancy theorem in their inspected material. Repeated searches for the Kneser, intersecting-family, Johnson-incidence and static-family aliases found no equivalent or dominating statement. Related published Kneser-pair results instead concern static domination, eigenpolytopes, or homotopy, which do not determine permitted slide sequences or distances. Unindexed or unpublished equivalent results remain an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: A differently worded or unindexed article might contain an equivalent reconfiguration theorem; no search can establish global uniqueness.
Some related scientific records were accessible as indexed summaries, not their full content; summary-level comparison is not represented as a full-text exclusion.

value.rationale: The \(k=3\) layer is a natural first nontrivial threshold where a pairwise-intersecting family may be either a star or a triangle, producing a Johnson-incidence geodesic law. The immediate collapse into isolated states at \(k=4\) is a sharp structural phase transition in feasible graph motion; the two-token diameter stays 4 for arbitrarily growing Kneser graphs. Exact radii, diameters and unexpectedly equal edge counts for the \(k=2\) and \(k=3\) moving layers yield natural benchmarks for distinguishing static intersecting-family geometry from dynamic token sliding. The contribution is an all-n, all-occupancy structural/metric theorem, not a parameter substitution or static known-table recensus.
